ptr.note: Allocator alloc2(opaque, size), called by av_buffer_pool_get under the pool mutex (serialized, any thread) whenever no free entry exists; NULL selects av_buffer_alloc. Results must be NULL or a sole, writable reference whose AVBuffer data holds at least size bytes, releasable by its own free callback on any thread. pool_alloc_buffer copies the result's data/opaque/free into the BufferPoolEntry but leaves its AVBuffer flags_internal, so a result that is BUFFER_FLAG_REALLOCATABLE (av_buffer_realloc of an empty slot, or a buffer av_buffer_realloc's copy path made) hands out a first pool buffer that av_buffer_realloc resizes IN PLACE: av_realloc frees or shrinks the block the entry still records, which the pool later recycles (use after free) and frees again at flush (double free). The C contract does not forbid such a result. Rust: BufferPool::with_allocator (FnMut(usize) -> Option<UninitBuffer>, allocator buffers from BufferReference::alloc/alloc_resizable or UninitBuffer::from_owner); its resize wrappers copy any buffer with an opaque, so pool buffers never reach the in-place path.

User state stored in pool->opaque, passed to every alloc call and to pool_free(opaque) once the pool is actually freed (after av_buffer_pool_uninit and the return of every outstanding buffer). Ownership moves to the pool when pool_free is non-NULL and the call succeeds; on a NULL return pool_free is never called and the caller keeps it. Never dereferenced by C. Rust: a Box<F> leaked into the pool and dropped by the pool_free trampoline, or here when init2 fails.
Opaque releaser, called exactly once by buffer_pool_free on the thread releasing the pool's last reference, after every entry was flushed; never called on a failed init. May be NULL.
As av_buffer_pool_init: a fresh pool, refcount 1, released by av_buffer_pool_uninit; NULL on failure. Rust: BufferPoolBox.
